This is a phase 3, randomized, double-blind multicenter study to evaluate safety and efficacy of ixazomib versus placebo in patients with relapsed and/or refractory multiple myeloma who were treated with lenalidomide and dexamethasone as their standard therapy.

design.text: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, multicenter, placebo-controlled study comparing oral ixazomib plus lenalidomide and dexamethasone versus placebo plus lenalidomide and dexamethasone; patients randomized 1:1.

Patients treated with lenalidomide plus dexamethasone were randomized 1:1 to receive ixazomib or placebo in a double-blind fashion.

On July 10, 2015 Millennium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Millennium) submitted a NDA for NINLARO (ixazomib) capsules, an orally bioavailable, small molecule inhibitor of the 20S proteasome, for the treatment of patients with multiple myeloma (MM) who have received at least one prior therapy.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) are diarrhea, constipation, thrombocytopenia, peripheral neuropathy, nausea, peripheral edema, vomiting, and back pain. Diarrhea occurred in 42% vs 36% placebo, constipation 34% vs 25%, nausea 26% vs 21%, vomiting 22% vs 11%, peripheral edema 25% vs 18%, rash 19% vs 11%. Serious adverse reactions in ≥2% included thrombocytopenia (2%) and diarrhea (2%).

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 20\%) are diarrhea, constipation, thrombocytopenia, peripheral neuropathy, nausea, peripheral edema, vomiting, and back pain. (6,1)

Diarrhea was reported in 42% of patients in the NINLARO regimen and 36% in the placebo regimen, constipation in 34% and 25%, respectively, nausea in 26% and 21%, respectively, and vomiting in 22% and 11%, respectively.
Peripheral edema was reported in 25% and 18% of patients in the NINLARO and placebo regimens, respectively.
Rash was reported in 19% of patients in the NINLARO regimen and 11% of patients in the placebo regimen.
Serious adverse reactions reported in \ge 2\% of patients included thrombocytopenia (2%) and diarrhea (2%).
